S1.name: Lateral Step-Down — low support, light
S1.execution: Bodyweight first; a light dumbbell only if still easy. Lower **3 s**, lightly touch the free heel, return under control. Rest **30 s between legs; 45 s before S2**.
S1.regress: Rehearse the plant leg controlling knee travel and pelvic position during weight acceptance. Use the lowest stable support that permits a level pelvis and whole stance-foot contact; use hand support if needed. Reduce step height/load for knee collapse or pelvic drop.
S1.alternative: If the step is unsuitable, use instead a hand-supported shallow single-leg squat, the same 1 × 4 per leg and easy effort.

S2.name: Short-Foot Drill — supported standing hold
S2.execution: **5 s relaxed reset** between holds, **30 s between feet**, **60 s before P1**. Stand with most weight on the working foot and fingertip support.
S2.regress: Strengthen active arch control while maintaining heel, big-toe base and little-toe base contact for planting. Keep toes long; do not roll onto the outside edge. Use bilateral weight support instead if arch control needs toe-clawing or ankle rolling.

P1.name: Split Squat — two dumbbells, both feet on floor
P1.execution: **3 s down**, smooth forceful rise; 2–3 RIR. Rest **60 s between legs, 120 s between rounds**.
P1.regress: Keep full front-foot pressure and knee travel aligned with the foot. Reduce load/range for heel lift, knee drift or trunk collapse.

P2.name: Romanian Deadlift — two dumbbells
P2.execution: bilateral; **2 s down**, purposeful hip extension; 2–3 RIR. Rest **120 s between working sets**.
P2.regress: Maintain a softly bent, nearly constant knee angle, weights close and a controlled back position; stop lowering at the owned range.

P3.name: Lateral Lunge — goblet dumbbell
P3.execution: step out, lower **2 s**, push back to the original stance; 2–3 RIR. Rest **60 s between legs**.
P3.regress: Keep the lunging foot grounded and knee aligned; sit into that hip without rotating away. Reduce width, depth or load for loss of control.

P4.name: Glute Bridge Iso Hold — long-lever hamstring variant
P4.execution: bilateral. Heels farther from the hips than a standard bridge, knees still bent; bodyweight or a securely hand-held sandbag over the pelvis to reach the holding-effort target.
P4.regress: Try to pull the heels toward the body without sliding them; keep ribs down. Bring heels closer or remove load for cramp/lost height; stop for symptoms.

P5.name: Copenhagen Side Plank — short lever
P5.execution: top knee/lower thigh on a stable bench, lower leg clear. Rest **60 s between sides**. Use bodyweight; if already controlled and too easy, secure a small dumbbell at the upper hip with the upper hand to reach the holding-effort target.
P5.regress: Keep shoulder comfortable and pelvis level. Use light lower-foot assistance if needed; stop for groin/shoulder pain or loss of position.
P5.alternative: If no suitable stable Copenhagen support fits, use instead floor side-lying hip adduction, upper foot on the floor in front, 1 × 8 per lower leg at 2–3 RIR with 60 s between sides; add a small hand-secured dumbbell above the inner knee only if needed and comfortable. Its preparation is 1 × 4 easy reps per leg instead of the hold ramps. This proposed replacement adds 16 dynamic working reps and removes 30 s of working holds; preparation adds 8 reps and removes 10 s of holds. Bouts are unchanged; allow up to 2 extra minutes.

P6.name: Bent-Knee Soleus Raise — seated, dumbbells on thighs
P6.execution: bilateral; knees near 90°, forefeet on floor, **1 s at top, 2 s lowering, quiet bottom reset**; 2–3 RIR. Rest **90 s between sets**.
P6.regress: Secure the weights above the knees, maintain knee angle and repeatable heel rise. Reduce load if heel height falls or bouncing replaces muscle force.
P6.alternative: For seated calf work, use a securely held sandbag instead of dumbbells when its shape and load fit better.

reverse.name: Reverse Lunge — two dumbbells
reverse.execution: Step backward under control, lower 2 s and drive through the original front foot to return. Keep knee tracking with the foot.
reverse.rest: Rest 60 s between legs, 120 s between rounds.
reverse.regress: Reduce step length/load for an uncontrolled backward reach or front-heel lift.

goblet.name: Goblet Squat
goblet.execution: Dumbbell held close; lower 3 s through owned range and stand decisively with both feet grounded.
goblet.regress: Reduce load/depth if the trunk folds or heels lift.

stepup.name: Step-Up — dumbbells
stepup.execution: Choose a stable box low enough to rise without a trailing-foot push. Whole working foot stays on top; lower 2 s.
stepup.rest: Rest 60 s between legs, 120 s between rounds.
stepup.regress: Lower support or load for pelvic hike, push-off from the floor or uncontrolled descent.
stepup.alternative: If no suitable stable box exists, use instead the floor split squat at the same side dose/effort and preparation dose; log the replacement.

hipthrust.name: Hip Thrust — dumbbell
hipthrust.execution: Upper back on a stable bench, dumbbell secured over pelvis; rise to hip extension without arching the back, lower 2 s.
hipthrust.regress: Reduce load/range for lumbar extension or hamstring cramp.
hipthrust.alternative: If bench geometry is unsuitable, use instead a loaded dynamic floor glute bridge at the same rep/effort and preparation dose.

slrdl.name: Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift — supported dumbbell
slrdl.execution: Light fingertip support; hold dumbbell in opposite hand, keep pelvis level and hinge 2 s down through controlled range.
slrdl.regress: Reduce range/load when pelvis opens; support should remove balance as the load limiter.

standingcalf.name: Standing Calf Raise — supported dumbbell
standingcalf.execution: Nearly straight working knee, light hand support, 1 s at top and 2 s lowering to the floor.
standingcalf.regress: Reduce load for bouncing or shortened heel rise.

airplane.name: Hip Airplane — supported
airplane.execution: Bodyweight, hand support and slight hip hinge. Slowly open/close pelvis through a small owned arc without rolling the stance foot.
airplane.rest: Keep easy; rest 30 s between legs.
airplane.regress: Reduce arc or use more hand support if knee/foot rotates uncontrollably.

bandwalk.name: Mini-Band Lateral Walk
bandwalk.execution: Very light loop above knees; small quiet steps, toes forward and knees aligned. Both directions are one set round.
bandwalk.regress: Use a lighter band/smaller step if pelvis sways or the task burns.

eversion.name: Seated Band Ankle Eversion — self-anchored (proposed)
eversion.execution: Sit securely, use the other foot to hold a light loop; turn the working forefoot slightly outward against tension, 2 s return, keep knee still.
eversion.regress: Use less tension/range for toe gripping or whole-leg rotation.
eversion.source: Proposed exact setup; no verified identifier
eversion.alternative: Use instead of the band, gentle hand resistance at the outer forefoot with the same easy reps if a loop cannot be secured.

adductorlight.name: Side-Lying Hip Adduction — light control (proposed)
adductorlight.execution: Top foot supported on floor in front; lift the straight lower leg a small distance, pause 1 s and lower 2 s. Bodyweight and easy effort.
adductorlight.regress: Shorten lever by bending the working knee if control becomes tiring.
adductorlight.source: Proposed exact light prescription; no verified identifier
